question.problem:
Suppose ${b}_{2}=k{b}_{1}-a$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2}=0.$ If $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and ${b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$, find the value of $k.$ 

*Hint: You might wish to take the equation ${b}_{2}=k{b}_{1}-a$ and find the dot product of both sides with ${b}_{1}.$*
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the equation ${b}_{2}=k{b}_{1}-a$ and find the dot product of both sides with ${b}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{2} & =k{b}_{1}-a \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & ={b}_{1}\cdot (k{b}_{1}-a) \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & ={b}_{1}\cdot (k{b}_{1})-({b}_{1}\cdot a) \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & =k({b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1})-({b}_{1}\cdot a)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the formula for the dot product to compute the values of ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1} & ={b}_{1}^{2}+{b}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2}+{0}^{2} \\  & =4 \\ {b}_{1}\cdot a & ={b}_{1}{a}_{1}+{b}_{2}{a}_{2} \\  & =2\cdot 1+0\cdot (-1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the values for ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1},$ ${b}_{1}\cdot a,$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & =k({b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1})-({b}_{1}\cdot a) \\ 0 & =k\cdot 4-2 \\ -4k & =-2 \\ k & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
